title: Balanced binary tree: subtree heights differ by at most 1 at every node
summary: The tree is asymmetric but meets the balance condition at every node.
context: The box on the right defines d as left subtree height minus right subtree height. Every node must satisfy |d| ≤ 1. Here d measures height difference, not node degree. Heights count edges, with 0 for a leaf and −1 for an empty subtree.
description: The tree on the left has four levels and 8 nodes with no value labels. The root’s left child has a left leaf and no right subtree. Its label is d = 1.

The root’s right child has two children. Its left child is internal and has two leaves, while its right child is itself a leaf. The root’s right child is labeled d = 1 and its left child d = 0. All four leaves have two empty subtrees and are labeled d = 0.
result: To determine balance, check every node. Checking only the root’s height difference is insufficient.

frames.title: Balanced binary tree: subtree heights differ by at most 1 at every node
frames.explanation: The root’s left subtree has height 1 and its right subtree height 2, so the root is labeled d = −1. Every other node’s height difference is also at most 1 in absolute value, so the tree is balanced.
